extracted.intended_audience: securities exchanges, listed-fund issuers, market participants, investors, and interested commenters to the SEC
extracted.subtask_short: listing options on crypto commodity trusts
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and procedural standards for listing and continued approval of options on Commodity-Based Trusts that hold one or multiple crypto assets, as proposed by MIAX Sapphire to amend Exchange Rules 402 and 403. Covers initial listing criteria, calculation methods, continued listing monitoring, trading mechanics, and surveillance/system requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic listing standards for Commodity-Based Trust Shares
rubrics_metrics.description: Shares of a 'Commodity-Based Trust' are defined by generic listing standards that the Trust: (1) is issued by a trust, LLC, partnership, or similar entity (and, if applicable, is operated by a registered commodity pool operator pursuant to the CEA) and is not registered as an investment company under the Investment Company Act of 1940; (2) is designed to reflect the performance of one or more reference assets or an index of reference assets; (3) to reflect performance, is issued by a Trust that holds (a) one or more commodities or commodity-based assets, and (b) in addition to such commodities or commodity-based assets, may hold securities, cash, and cash equivalents; (4) is issued by such Trust in a specified aggregate minimum number in return for a deposit of (a) a specified quantity of the underlying commodities, commodity-based assets, securities, cash, and/or cash equivalents or (b) a cash amount with a value based on the next determined net asset value per Trust share; and (5) when aggregated in the same specified minimum number, may be redeemed at a holder's request by the Trust which will deliver to the redeeming holder (a) the specified quantity of the underlying commodities, commodity-based assets, securities, cash, and/or cash equivalents or (b) a cash amount with a value based on the next determined net asset value per Trust share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These generic listing standards (adopted by primary listing markets) form the baseline eligibility for Commodity-Based Trust Shares to be treated as equity securities and eligible for ETF-style listing and trading; options may be listed on trusts that meet these generic standards in addition to the Exchange-specific criteria in Rule 402.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market value threshold for each underlying crypto asset (402(i)(6)(iii)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: The total global supply of each underlying crypto asset(s) held by the Commodity-Based Trust must have an average daily market value of at least $700 million over the last 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to each crypto asset individually when a trust holds multiple crypto assets. The Exchange proposes to verify this criterion on a monthly basis as part of continued listing obligations; the Exchange believes monthly verification is reasonable given typical market-cap inertia and administrative burden of daily calculation (document provides example calculations showing resilience to short-term swings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivatives-market surveillance requirement for each crypto asset (402(i)(6)(iii)(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each crypto asset held by the Commodity-Based Trust must underlie a derivatives contract that trades on a market with which the Exchange has a comprehensive surveillance sharing agreement, whether directly or through common membership in the Intermarket Surveillance Group (ISG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange proposes to monitor this requirement continuously (daily). The requirement is intended to provide access to surveillance information to detect/manipulative conduct; examples of applicable markets include CME and Coinbase Derivatives (both ISG members). The Exchange must ensure the requirement is met prior to listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'crypto asset' for rule purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the rule the term 'crypto asset' means an asset that is generated, issued and/or transferred using a blockchain or similar distributive ledger technology network, including but not limited to, assets known as 'tokens,' 'digital assets,' 'virtual currencies,' and 'coins' and that relies on cryptographic protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definitional language clarifies the universe of instruments subject to the $700 million market-cap and derivatives-surveillance criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market value calculation method (total supply × token price)
rubrics_metrics.description: The market value for each underlying crypto asset held by a Commodity-Based Trust will be calculated by taking the total global supply of the particular crypto asset multiplied by the token price of that asset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total supply includes all currently issued tokens and does not include unissued tokens (example given with Bitcoin). Market supply information can be obtained from publicly available sources such as coingecko.com or coinmarketcap.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total supply definition (issued vs. maximum/unissued)
rubrics_metrics.description: The total supply of a crypto asset includes all crypto assets currently issued and does not include unissued crypto assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for Bitcoin the Exchange would use current total supply (e.g., 20,000,406) rather than maximum supply (21,000,000) when calculating market value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued listing monitoring frequencies and standards (Rule 403(g) amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: For options covering ETFs approved under Exchange Rule 402(i)(6): (i) the $700 million average daily market value criterion (402(i)(6)(iii)(A)) will be assessed by the Exchange on a monthly basis; and (ii) the derivatives contract surveillance criterion (402(i)(6)(iii)(B)) will be assessed on a daily (continuous) basis. If either criterion is no longer satisfied, the Exchange may treat that as a basis for withdrawal of approval/opening additional series restrictions or delisting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monthly monitoring rationale: unlikely that an asset with a 12-month average daily market value ≥ $700M would fall below the threshold in a short period; example provided showing large tolerances to short-term drops. The Exchange may also consider other continued-listing factors and discretionary actions per Rule 403(g)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Exchange Rule 403 continued-listing triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: ETFs approved for options trading will not be deemed to meet continued-approval requirements, and the Exchange shall not open additional series, if the ETFs are delisted from trading pursuant to Exchange Rule 403(b)(4), are halted or suspended from trading in their primary market, or if other events/conditions render further dealing inadvisable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchange Rule 403(g)(5) permits the Exchange to suspend open transactions or delist if, in the Exchange's opinion, events make continued dealing inadvisable; Exchange may delist options lacking sufficient liquidity or market demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that each underlying crypto asset satisfy criteria in multi-asset trusts
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Commodity-Based Trust holds multiple crypto assets, the criteria in Exchange Rule 402(i)(6)(iii)(A) and (B) (market value threshold and derivatives-surveillance agreement) must be met for each underlying crypto asset individually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed 402(i)(6) amendment explicitly extends the per-asset requirements to multi-asset trusts; the Exchange will calculate each asset's market value separately and verify surveillance linkages for each asset's derivative market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial listing procedural requirement (reliance on primary listing market generic standards plus Exchange Rule 402)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Commodity-Based Trust may qualify for options listing on the Exchange if it meets the generic listing standards of the applicable primary listing market and also satisfies Exchange Rule 402(a) and (b), or Exchange Rule 402(i)(6)(i)(B) (as applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange may list options on qualifying Commodity-Based Trusts without additional Commission approvals once the initial listing criteria are met—consistent with how options on other ETFs are listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening of option series expirations and permitted durations (Exchange Rule 404/406)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange will open at least one expiration month for options on Commodity-Based Trusts and may list series for weekly, monthly, or quarterly expirations. The Exchange may also list LEAPS that expire from 12 to 39 months from listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monthly expirations are subject to the listing criteria in Exchange Rule 404 and its Interpretations and Policies; additional series may be opened to maintain orderly markets or meet customer demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strike price interval standards and Short Term Options Series rules (Exchange Rule 404 Interpretation .06)
rubrics_metrics.description: Strike price intervals for series of options on ETFs must be reasonably close to the price per share of the underlying security at the time series is first opened, or be consistent with intervals established on another options exchange. For Short Term Option Series, during the month prior to expiration the strike price intervals for the related non-Short Term Option must match the Short Term Option intervals. Specific permitted short-term strike intervals include: (i) $0.50 or greater where strike < $100, and $1 or greater where strike is between $100 and $150; (ii) $0.50 for option classes that trade in one dollar increments and are in the Short Term Option Series Program; or (iii) $2.50 or greater where strike is above $150.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange may also list series pursuant to the $1 Strike Price Interval Program, the $0.50 Strike Program, and the $2.50 Strike Price Program as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum pricing increment for options (Exchange Rule 510)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the price of a series of options on a Commodity-Based Trust is less than $3.00, the minimum increment will be $0.05; where the price is $3.00 or higher, the minimum increment will be $0.10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These minimum increments are consistent with the increments for options on other ETFs listed on the Exchange and apply to any new series listed for Commodity-Based Trusts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position and exercise limit methodology (MIAX Rules 307 and 309)
rubrics_metrics.description: Position and exercise limits for options on Commodity-Based Trusts are determined pursuant to MIAX Rules 307 and 309 and vary according to number of outstanding shares and trading volumes of the underlying ETF over the past six months. The largest and most frequently traded ETFs have limits of 250,000 contracts (with adjustments for splits, re-capitalizations, etc.); smaller ETFs have limits of 200,000, 75,000, 50,000, or 25,000 contracts on the same side of the market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits are comparable to limits applied to other ETF options on the Exchange and include customary adjustments for corporate actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Margin requirements applicability (Exchange Rule 1502)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchange Rule 1502, which governs margin requirements applicable to trading on the Exchange (including options on ETFs), will apply to options on Commodity-Based Trusts listed pursuant to Exchange Rule 402(i)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Margin treatment is the same as for other ETF options; firms and customers must comply with applicable margin rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surveillance program and systems capacity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange must have surveillance procedures and systems capacity to support listing and trading of options on qualifying Commodity-Based Trusts, including real-time patterns for price and volume movements and post-trade surveillance patterns (e.g., spoofing, marking the close, pinging, phishing). The Exchange represents that OPRA and the Exchange have necessary capacity to handle additional traffic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchange must have comprehensive surveillance sharing agreements (directly or via ISG) with markets trading derivatives tied to the crypto assets. The surveillance program is intended to deter and detect manipulative behavior; the Exchange may obtain information from designated contract markets that are ISG members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of public data sources for market-supply information
rubrics_metrics.description: Market supply information for crypto assets can be obtained from publicly available sources such as coingecko.com or coinmarketcap.com for purposes of calculating market value and satisfying the $700 million threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange cites these publicly available sources as data inputs for calculating total supply × token price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange discretion to delist for liquidity or demand reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange may determine at any point to delist an option on a Commodity-Based Trust that may not have sufficient liquidity or market demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This discretionary power complements the objective continued-listing criteria and permits the Exchange to act where market conditions warrant removal of option listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of all existing ETF options trading rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Options on Commodity-Based Trusts approved under Exchange Rule 402(i)(6) will trade in the same manner as options on other ETFs; existing Exchange Rules that govern listing criteria, expirations, exercise prices, minimum increments, position and exercise limits, margin requirements, customer accounts and trading halt procedures will apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listing and trading mechanics are intended to be consistent with the broader ETF options framework on the Exchange to promote uniform treatment and investor protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to satisfy Exchange Rule 402 continued-listing provisions for certain listings
rubrics_metrics.description: For ETFs listed pursuant to Exchange Rule 402(i)(6)(i)(A), the Exchange proposes to require continued satisfaction of the requirements in Exchange Rule 403 subparagraphs (b)(1), (2), (3) and (4) in addition to the new 402(i)(6)(iii) criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ties the new crypto-asset-specific continued-listing checks into the Exchange's existing continued-listing framework for underlying securities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural availability of options listing without additional Commission approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: The Exchange proposes that permitting Commodity-Based Trust Shares (including those holding multiple crypto assets) to be listed and traded without the need for additional approvals will allow the Exchange to immediately list and trade qualifying options once the initial listing criteria have been met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors how most ETFs can list options once initial listing criteria are satisfied and is justified as removing impediments to a free and open market and facilitating investor hedging and price discovery.
